newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares inch up, Reliance off on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: India shares inch up, Reliance off on profit-taking.

text.p: Indian stock prices crawled ahead on Friday amid lacklustre trade as a result of end-account considerations, traders said.
But share prices could push higher next week on support from foreign funds in index-linked stocks, they said.
The Bombay share index ended this week 50.20 points, or over one percent, higher at 4,133.24, thus gaining 11 percent in the last five straight weeks.
They said shares of bellwether Reliance Industries fell victim to a sharp bout of institutional profit-taking after the firm's liberal one for one bonus share announcement.
Reliance tumbled 10.25 rupees, or nearly three percent, to end near the day's low at 367.0 with 7.50 million shares changing hands at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
"That there was a lot of profit-booking in the stock," said Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Capital India.
"End-account factors also obviously affected the price."

Reliance shares hit a new 52-week high of 388.0 on Thursday after the company announced a liberal one-for-one bonus share issue, suprising market participants. But heavy offloading by foreign institutions capped the price rise.
